text:
Sam: quick brain dump — I'm proposing we introduce an explicit 'deferred-ack' signal from upstream services for streaming requests where the model/runtime has accepted the request but isn't ready to emit tokens yet. current approach is opaque to clients and makes retries and backpressure awkward.

Anya: can you sketch how that differs from our current 202 Accept / 204 behaviors?

Sam: right now gateway passes through 202 or just keeps the socket open. deferred-ack would be a short header-first response that still leaves the stream open but tells the edge: accepted + estimated work. useful for client UX and retry policies. example headers:

```
X-Edge-Ack: deferred
X-Edge-Ack-Estimate-MS: 1200
X-Edge-Ack-ID: abc123
```

Devon: hmm. does that change billing or SLA semantics? if we ack early we might start charging sooner.

Sam: good call. proposal: billing window starts on token emission; ack only affects routing/backpressure decisions and idempotency bookkeeping. we keep separate lifecycle timestamps: ack_ts vs first_token_ts vs finish_ts.

Morgan: how would retries work? deferred ack can lead clients to assume request will complete and not retry, which is good, but we still need robust server-side hedging.

Sam: two-layer retry model: client-side (based on idempotency key + ack) and edge-side hedging. clients should only retry if no ack seen within X ms OR if ack indicates a terminal failure. edge hedging can use the ack as signal to avoid duplicate work: if ack exists, hedges should be limited to metadata-only probes that don't rerun expensive work.

Leo: we need a way to express idempotency modes so downstreams can opt into safe retries vs forbid. header idea: `X-Idempotency-Mode: safe|no-retry|hedge-allowed`

Irene: will downstreams have to change code? that's a lot. Maybe make gateway synthesize the useful signals from existing runtime states first, then roll a small opt-in header.

Sam: agreed — fallback: gateway can infer deferred-ack from runtime lifecycle (accepted + queue-pos > 0). opt-in header expands expressivity.

Anya: what about failure windows and streaming abort semantics? current client cancels -> we propagate a cancel and tear down. can we support a 'graceful detach' where the gateway informs upstream it's detaching but allows in-flight token emission for N ms to finish and be captured?

Devon: that sounds like the 'linger on cancel' feature we've talked about. tradeoff: resource hold vs better tail-quality. propose configurable window per route: `detach_grace_ms` with hard cap.

Sam: example config snippet: 

```
route:
  detach_grace_ms: 250
  ack_timeout_ms: 800
  idempotency_default: safe
```

Morgan: observability: we need metrics: ack_latency, ack_to_first_token, detach_grace_used, hedged_probe_count. also label by idempotency-mode.

OpsBot: deploy scheduled: staging/edge-proxy v2.3.0 -> 2025-06-12T03:00Z (rolling). No downtime expected. :shipit:

Irene: please also add an event to tracing that links ack_id -> final request_id so we can correlate. otherwise debugging will be messy.

Sam: +1. also add a short-lived KV for ack_id -> route/tenant to help ingress routers avoid duplicate start. TTL=30s default.

Anya: concerns: some runtimes might mistake deferred-ack for completed acceptance and drop hedges entirely. doc it well and provide a compatibility mode that treats `X-Edge-Ack` as advisory.

Leo: security note: ack_id should be opaque and unguessable. avoid exposing internal queue positions.

Devon: ok — next steps: write short RFC with: header shapes, billing semantics, detach_grace config, metrics & tracing, and a migration plan where gateway synthesizes ack first. volunteers to draft?

Sam: I can draft the RFC today. will include sample flows and a sequence diagram.

Morgan: I'll own the metrics + dashboards work.

Irene: i'll add tracing instrumentation plan and ack_id correlation table on the infra side.

Anya: i'll review and add compatibility guidance for downstreams.

Sam: awesome — thanks. tagging @here for visibility.

OpsBot: note: new issue created: infra/arch #4127 "deferred-ack signal & detach_grace proposal" by Sam.

Sam: leaving this here — if anyone has strong objections speak up in the RFC thread. otherwise i'll post the first draft by EOD. :+1:
